transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love—my workshop, church, even fishing don’t mean anything to me right now. My wife and my pastor were really worried about me and encouraged me to come in and talk to someone.
Have you ever had periods in your life where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or productive, to the point where you didn't need much sleep for several days?

No, I have never experienced periods like that in my life. I've always been a pretty steady, even-keeled person, and I've certainly never felt unusually energetic or gone without sleep. Honestly, it's quite the opposite for me.
Have you recently experienced any significant changes in your physical health, such as a head injury, new medical conditions, or starting any new medications?

No head injuries or new medications, but my primary doctor recently raised concerns about possible mild cognitive impairment and ordered some testing. He also told me to cut back on driving and my usual activities, which has been a devastating blow to my independence. It really shook me to my core.
Have you noticed any other physical symptoms or changes in your memory, focus, or personality that began around the same time as these feelings of sadness?

Yes, my mind feels like it's in a frustrating, foggy blur now—I constantly lose my train of thought mid-sentence and struggle to make simple decisions like what shirt to wear. Physically, I've slowed down to a crawl, taking forever just to get dressed, and my wife constantly asks if I'm sick because I'm shuffling around the house so much.
Did you notice the 'foggy' thinking and difficulty with decisions starting before you felt this deep sadness, or did the sadness and loss of interest come first?

It’s a bit of both, honestly. The minor forgetfulness and misplacing tools started first, about six months into my retirement, which is what led to the doctor's visit in the first place. But this deep sadness, the loss of interest, and that overwhelming, foggy indecisiveness really only took hold over the last three weeks, right after the doctor brought up the memory testing.
When you have these 'foggy' moments, are they constant throughout the day, or do you find that your ability to think clearly fluctuates significantly from one hour to the next?
I'm not quite sure about the exact timing, to be honest, as I haven't paid close attention to when it fluctuates. It just feels like a heavy, frustrating blur that hangs over me most of the day.

Since your memory concerns began, have you experienced any times of day where you are completely clear-headed and back to your usual self, or has this 'fog' been present every single day since it started?

No, I haven't had any times where I feel like my old, clear-headed self anymore. This fog has been pretty much constant every single day since it took hold about three weeks ago. It all just blends together into a continuous, frustrating blur.

If you look back to the months before the sadness started, were you able to perform your daily tasks like managing finances or following complex instructions as well as you could a few years ago, or was there already a noticeable decline in those abilities?

Before the deep sadness hit, I was still trying to manage, but I definitely noticed some minor lapses like misplacing my tools, leaving the stove on, or losing my train of thought while mentoring. Those early struggles are what led my doctor to bring up mild cognitive impairment, which triggered all this worry and the much more intense, foggy feeling I've had over the last three weeks.

When you perform tasks like managing your finances or following instructions, do you find that you are genuinely unable to remember how to do them, or is it more that you feel too unmotivated or discouraged to try?

It’s really a mix of both. Early on, I had some genuine lapses like leaving the stove on, but lately, it’s more that I feel too foggy, discouraged, and useless to even try focusing on tasks like managing our bills, so I just rely on my wife to handle them.

If you were to set aside your feelings of sadness and discouragement for a moment, do you feel that your memory and thinking difficulties have continued to worsen progressively over the last few months, or have they stayed about the same?

The forgetfulness and lapses in attention started gradually a few months ago after I retired, which is what led to my doctor raising concerns. But over the last three weeks, it feels like it has gotten significantly worse and more overwhelming, turning into a constant, frustrating fog where I lose my train of thought and struggle with simple decisions. It's really hard to tell now what is just a memory issue and what is this overall cloudiness.

If you were given a simple task that you once knew well, would you be unable to remember the steps entirely, or do you find that you know how to do it but simply cannot focus long enough to complete it?

It is definitely the second option. I still know how to do things, but my mind gets incredibly foggy and I lose my train of thought halfway through, making it impossible to focus or make simple decisions. It’s just this frustrating, foggy blur that makes me feel completely useless.
Have you noticed any changes in your walking, such as a slower, more shuffling gait, or any new stiffness in your muscles that occurred alongside these memory and mood changes?

Yes, my wife has definitely noticed me moving much slower and shuffling around the house, to the point where she constantly asks if I'm feeling sick. It takes me forever just to do simple things like get dressed, and I often find myself sitting completely still and staring at things for minutes at a time, though I haven't noticed any actual stiffness in my muscles.
Have you noticed any new tremors, shaking in your hands, or have you experienced any unusual vivid dreams where you might be acting out your dreams or talking in your sleep?
No, I haven't experienced any shaking or tremors in my hands. I also haven't had any unusual, vivid dreams, and my wife hasn't said anything about me acting them out or talking in my sleep.

If your wife were to help you structure your day with clear reminders and encouragement, do you feel you would be able to complete those daily tasks, or do you find that the 'fog' prevents you from recalling the steps entirely?

My wife is actually already trying to help me by reminding me to eat, take my medicine, and pay the bills, but the fog is still a major barrier. Everything just blends together into a frustrating blur where I lose my train of thought or get stuck on simple decisions like what to wear. Even with her encouragement, actually completing tasks feels incredibly difficult.

When you are having one of these 'foggy' moments, are you able to recall recent events or conversations if you are given a hint or a reminder, or do you find that the information is completely lost from your memory?

I'm not entirely sure, and I haven't really paid close enough attention to know if hints help me recall things. In those moments, everything just feels like a frustrating, foggy blur where I completely lose my train of thought.
When you struggle to recall something, does it feel like the information is completely gone from your mind, or is it more that you cannot access it until someone provides a hint or a reminder?

I'm not entirely sure how to describe it, and I can't really pinpoint if a hint would help or not. It just feels like a foggy, frustrating blur where I lose my train of thought completely. Everything just goes blank in those moments, so it's hard to tell.

When you struggle to remember something, do you find that if someone gives you a hint or a clue, the information comes back to you, or does the information seem to be completely missing from your memory regardless of any help?

I'm really not sure if hints help, as I haven't paid close enough attention to notice. When I lose my train of thought or forget something, it just feels like a frustrating, foggy blur and I can't seem to grasp it anyway.

If I were to give you a list of three simple words to remember and ask you to repeat them back after a few minutes, do you think you could recall them if I gave you a hint for each one, or do you think the words would be completely gone from your mind?

I honestly doubt I could remember them right now. With this constant brain fog and how often I've been losing my train of thought or misplacing things, I feel like I would struggle or completely forget the words. It makes me really anxious that I might be losing my mind, as everything has just become such a frustrating blur.

When you struggle to remember recent events, do you find that you are genuinely unable to store the new information at all, or is it that your mind is so preoccupied with feelings of sadness and worthlessness that you aren't paying enough attention to remember them?

I think it’s a mix of both, honestly. My mind is constantly in this foggy, frustrating blur where I easily lose my train of thought, but I'm also deeply weighed down by a heavy, hollow ache and this terrifying worry that I'm losing my mind. It makes it incredibly hard to focus or pay attention to anything else.
